newsitem.title: USA: Maine's jobless rate edges up to 4.8 pct in May.
newsitem.headline: Maine's jobless rate edges up to 4.8 pct in May.

text.p: Maine's jobless rate in May edged up a tenth of a percentage point to 4.8 percent as construction and tourism-driven industries started hiring ahead of summer, the state Labor Department said on Monday.

"However, the May 1997 unemployment rate of 4.8 percent was lower than the May 1996 rate of 5.2 percent, representing a decline in the number of unemployed from 34,900 to 32,000," said Valerie Landry, state labor commissioner, in prepared remarks.

Although seasonally adjusted nonfarm wage and salary employment was unchanged between April and May at 546,300, there was an increase of 7,400 jobs between May 1996 and May 1997. The biggest over-the-year gains were in services, wholesale trade and construction.

When measured on a not-seasonally adjusted basis, nonfarm wage and salary jobs rose seasonally by 12,300 from April to May. Normal seasonal employment gains were seen in construction, eating and drinking places and lodging services as summer drew near.
